title: I used GPT‑6 Astra and Blender to prototype an open world. Here’s the result
author: ImportantAd4397
selftext:
I’ve been experimenting with an AI-assisted workflow for building a castle-centered open-world environment.



GPT-6 Astra was used as a planning and problem-solving partner during the process, helping me explore the overall structure, break the environment into manageable sections, and iterate on parts of the Blender workflow. The actual scene was modeled, assembled, adjusted, and rendered in Blender.



This video shows the current environment pass: the castle as the main landmark, the surrounding terrain, and the routes and spaces that could eventually support exploration. It isn’t a finished or playable game level yet. The goal of this experiment was to see whether GPT-6 could help move a large 3D environment from a rough idea to a coherent model, and where manual 3D judgment would still become the bottleneck.



The hardest part has been balancing two different scales. The castle needs to have a strong silhouette and feel impressive from a distance, but the spaces around it also need to remain believable when viewed from a player’s perspective. AI suggestions were useful for generating possibilities, but proportions, composition, geometry cleanup, and visual consistency still required a lot of manual iteration in Blender.



I’d be interested to hear whether the castle works as a clear landmark, whether the surrounding environment makes you curious to explore, and which parts still feel procedural or visually disconnected.



This is an early modeling experiment, so honest and technical feedback is welcome.
